_comment: Where each Köppen climate class goes on vanilla's temperature and humidity bands (plan §7.2, P1-09). One file, two readers, like default.json beside it: the core (crates/deeptime-core/src/bake/placement.rs, include_str!) uses it as the bake's default, and the game ships it as data/deeptime/deeptime/climate_mapping/placement.json. A datapack may override it: at a dedicated server's first start FirstStartGenerator reads the pack's copy and hands it to the bake in the content bundle (key 'climate_placement'), so the bake places the world's climate by the pack's table; the table used is recorded in the world data (manifest notes.bake.climate.placement). Coordinates are band coordinates: temperature 0 to 5 over frozen | cold | temperate | warm | hot, humidity 0 to 5 over the five humidity bands (b = 2.5 is the middle of the third band). 'temperature_ramps' name a band coordinate as base + span * (the weighted sum of inputs, each a temperature clamped between its 'from' and 'to' and scaled to 0..1); 'humidity_rules' start from the aridity index's band coordinate (0.03, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5 -> 0 to 5 on a log scale) and squeeze it into 'squeeze' (band coordinate 1 to 4 mapped linearly onto [lo, hi]), then hold it at or above 'min' and at or below 'max'; 'classes' give every land class a temperature ramp (by name, or a 'when' switch on one input) and a humidity rule. Land above its equilibrium line (glaciated) is capped at 'glacier_cap', unless its class has a 'glaciated' block: that block (a temperature ramp and/or a humidity rule, each falling back to the class's ordinary one, uncapped) then decides for glaciated land. EF has one (Ben, 2026-09-29, 'Ice only where there's ice'): EF above its equilibrium line is ice cap (humidity band 0.5: ice spikes, frozen and jagged peaks, snowy slopes and plains), the rest of EF is barren frozen ground (humidity band 1.5: gravel and shrubland where the pack has them, thin snow where it has not); both sit at temperature band 0.6 to 0.8, the upper part of the frozen band, where Terralith puts its dry cold biomes (gravel desert, cold shrubland) rather than the red, terracotta snowy badlands it uses below band 0.5. P/PET says nothing in a freezing climate (PET is 0 below 0 C, so the index is pinned at 10), which is why EF takes fixed humidity rules (min = max). A class may also carry 'erosion': {min, max} (its land's erosion is clamped into it; vanilla's erosion units, -1 to 1; a glaciated block may give its own) and 'weirdness': 'positive' (its land takes the positive branch of the variant noise everywhere) or {'positive_below_erosion': e} (the positive branch where erosion is below e, the negative one above: high relief gets vanilla's frozen peaks, never the negative branch's jagged peaks or Terralith's scarlet mountains, and the flats get the negative branch, where vanilla's and Terralith's cherry groves, which are positive-branch variants, do not grow). EF uses all three (Ben, 2026-09-30): barren EF is held below erosion 0.3, which keeps it off Terralith's packed-ice glacial chasm (erosion 0.4 and up, or 0.565 and up at any humidity), ice cap keeps the chasm; its peaks are positive (erosion below -0.27: a little above vanilla's -0.375 edge, because MIC's Tectonic router stretches erosion, so that no negative-branch cell is left in the band Terralith's scarlet mountains use) and its flats negative except where the variant noise is above 0.2 (about a fifth of them), which are positive so that vanilla's ice spikes, a positive-branch variant, come back (Ben, 2026-09-30, 'Bring ice spikes back'); their |weirdness| is held to 0.25 at most, below where the cherry groves are (they need 0.4 and up at mid erosion, which is where MIC's router squashes everything from 0.3 to 0.57). 'ice_cover' (every key optional) is the snow and ice the game's surface pass lays on ground above its equilibrium line whatever the biome (Ben, 2026-09-30, 'Force snow/ice cover'; Terralith has no flat inland ice biome): a cover is 1 block where the land carries ice and one more per step_m metres of the climate's ice thickness (of height above the equilibrium line without ice fields) up to max_blocks; its top snow_blocks blocks are the snow block, the rest the ice block, and a cover of at least blue_ice_from_blocks blocks ends in blue_ice_blocks of the deep-ice block; the bake writes the thickness as the layer climate/ice_cover and records this section in notes.bake.climate.ice_cover. BWk is a cold desert when its mean annual temperature is 10 degC or less (Ben, 2026-10-02, 'classify them properly and if a mod a player brings has a better biome then swap to it. Otherwise just go with our best bet in terms of other cold bimoes'; BIO-101 to BIO-103): above 10 degC it is the hot desert (sand, badlands on plateaus); from 0 to 10 degC it is the driest land of the cold band (ramp cold_desert 1.05 to 1.95, humidity at most 0.6: vanilla's plains and meadow, Terralith's steppe, cold shrubland and temperate highlands); at or below 0 degC it is barren frozen ground like EF's (polar_ice, polar_desert: snowy plains in vanilla, Terralith's gravel desert and cold shrubland, Biomes O' Plenty's cold desert), because the mods that have a cold desert put it in the upper frozen band at the driest humidities. A 'temperature' or 'humidity' may be a {when, then, else} switch whose branches are again names or switches (four deep). Every one of the 31 land classes (Af to EF) must be present. Every ramp, rule and clamp here is a game choice (docs/science/ledger/BIO.md, BIO-026 to BIO-054, BIO-075 to BIO-081, BIO-101 to BIO-103), not a measurement; the only physical anchor is the aridity index's first three values (0.03, 0.2, 0.5: UNEP's hyper-arid, arid and semi-arid limits, BIO-038). FORMAT.md, 'The climate mapping', is the schema. A class may carry "cold_wetland": true: its wet, flat, low land is boreal peatland, not vanilla's swamp (taiga without a mod, the pack's bog or peatland biome where it has one; ledger BIO-104, BIO-106; Ben, decisions log 2026-10-03). The six subarctic classes have it; Dfa, Dfb and the C classes keep the swamp.
